text: The update packets MUST have the same RTP timestamp value as the initial packet for the event, but the duration MUST be increased to reflect the total cumulative duration since the beginning of the event.
notes: every forwarded packet of one event carries the timestamp the event start was mapped to on that leg; duration passed unchanged

text: The first packet for an event MUST have the M bit set.
notes: the M bit of a forwarded event packet is the M bit it came in with

text: The final packet for an event MUST have the E bit set, but setting of the "E" bit MAY be deferred until the final packet is retransmitted (see Section 2.5.1.4).
notes: the event payload (event code, E bit, volume, duration) is forwarded byte for byte

text: Intermediate packets for an event MUST NOT have either the M bit or the E bit set.
notes: intermediate packets go out with M=0 and their payload unchanged, so E stays clear

text: The final packet for each event and for each segment SHOULD be sent a total of three times at the interval used by the source for updates.
notes: each end-of-event retransmission that arrives is forwarded, none is collapsed

text: Once the sender has set the E bit for a packet, it MUST continue to set the E bit for any further retransmissions of that packet.
notes: retransmitted end packets keep their E bit on every forward

text: The RTP sequence number MUST be incremented by one in each successive RTP packet sent.
notes: on a leg, audio and forwarded event packets share one sequence that steps by one, retransmissions included

text: If the sender receives an "events" parameter from the receiver, it MUST restrict the set of events it sends to those listed in the received "events" parameter.
notes: only legs opened with a telephone-event payload type get events, and only the event codes that leg lists; an unknown payload type is still ignored

text: SDP descriptions using the event payload MUST contain an fmtp format attribute that lists the event values that the receiver can process.
notes: SDP content; signalling, not the mixer: chappe_sip_media_mix_sdp writes a=fmtp with the events next to telephone-event/8000

text: The RTCP attribute MAY be used as a media level attribute; it MUST NOT be used as a session level attribute.
notes: a leg given the port (and address) of a media-level a=rtcp sends its RTCP there and not to the RTP port + 1; the mixer writes no a=rtcp and the SDP side reads only a media-level one

text: The RTCP attribute SHOULD NOT be used for other applications.
notes: addressed to SDP writers; the mixer writes no a=rtcp
